AttributeError: asgiref.local._CVar object has no attribute 'value'
Running the latest `main` (`abc69a054aa440ef42c939b5a197df05c3ad48d2`) in production to test a fix for https://github.com/django/asgiref/issues/467, I see this error somewhat frequently across a wide spread of our requests/endpoints. This error was frequent enough that I reverted back to the old version which errors in a different way less frequently like https://github.com/django/asgiref/issues/467.

Not really sure why `__delattr__` in `_CVar` needs to throw if we try to delete an attribute that doesn't exist. Does this indicate a programming/synchronization bug somewhere or is this just a bit over-restricting? Not sure if this is bug prevention or its just fine.

Happy to test any further improvements/fixes here to try and get a release which doesn't have errors. Can also provide any additional info that might be helpful here if need be.

Linked arguments are not validated correctly on config dump
## 🕰️ Regression report

Starting from v4.37.0 (including the latest v.4.38.0), saving a config using ArgumentParser.save triggers an internal validation error when linked arguments are used.

### To reproduce

Using LightningCLI, follow the tutorial on argument linking.
https://lightning.ai/docs/pytorch/stable/cli/lightning_cli_expert.html#argument-linking

The issue happens when the SaveConfigCallback of LightningCLI tries to save the configuration. It is not triggered when using parse_args (the config is parsed correctly and the objects such as the model, loggers, datamodules, ... are correctly instantiated).

Version v4.36.0 works correctly when using the very same code.

Investigating a bit I found that in v4.36.0 the "target" value is correctly found in the ` val` and `ccfg` variables of [this part of the code](https://github.com/omni-us/jsonargparse/blob/b7eed539f71b6c1be3be40d3d1148af2d28e8dec/jsonargparse/_core.py#L1134), while the target value is not present in those vars starting from version v4.37.0.

### Prior behavior

Version v4.36.0 works correctly and SaveConfigCallback is able to save the configuration correctly.

PyTorch Lightning version: 2.5.1 (pip install)
jsonargparse: affected versions are v4.37/38.0 (pip install), v.36.0 works correctly

Completion for commands in nested groups is broken in Click 8.2.0
## Summary

In Click 8.2.0, completion for commands in nested groups doesn't work as expected anymore. Instead of completing command options and/or arguments, completion infinitely repeats the command names for the group.

## Example program

Inspired by the example in #2847 

Save the following as `bin/nested` in a virtualenv

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python

# nested

import click


def _complete_arg(ctx, _, incomplete):
    values = [
        "foo",
        "bar",
        "foobar",
        "baz",
    ]
    return [v for v in values if v.startswith(incomplete)]

@click.group
def main():
    ...

@main.group
def subgroup():
    ...

@subgroup.command
@click.option("--name", help="Name of something.")
@click.argument("arg", shell_complete=_complete_arg)
def compile(name: str | None, arg: str) -> None:
    """Test argument completion in nested groups."""
    click.echo(f"{name=} {arg=}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main.main()
```

Run `eval "$(_NESTED_COMPLETE=bash_source nested)"` to setup completion (for bash)

## Completion behavior

|Prefix|8.2.0 completion suggestions (unexpected behavior)|8.1.8 completion suggestions (expected behavior)|
|-|-|-|
|`nested`|`subgroup`|`subgroup`|
|`nested subgroup`|`compile`|`compile`|
|`nested subgroup compile`|`compile`|`foo     bar     foobar  baz`|
|`nested subgroup compile f`|none|`foo     foobar`|
|`nested subgroup compile --`|`--help`|`--name  --help`|
|`nested subgroup compile --name=n`|`compile`|`foo     bar     foobar  baz`|

## Environment

- Python version: Python 3.12.3
- Click version: 8.2.0

## Initial debugging

Reverting 0ef55fda47bb3d0dece21197d81d8d72a4250e73 for `src/click/shell_completion.py` restores the 8.1.8 completion behavior.

Looking at the change, I believe that the bug is actually caused by a simple statement reordering . IMO https://github.com/pallets/click/blob/af73ce4793bf38edf11a16e959ef0d8a0dbf6c1f/src/click/shell_completion.py#L567-L571 should be the following to preserve the 8.1.8 behavior:

```python
                    with cmd.make_context(
                        name, args, parent=ctx, resilient_parsing=True
                    ) as sub_ctx:
                        ctx = sub_ctx
                        args = ctx._protected_args + ctx.args
```

Note that Click 8.1.8 directly assigns `cmd.make_context()` to `ctx` in the equivalent snippet: https://github.com/pallets/click/blob/934813e4d421071a1b3db3973c02fe2721359a6e/src/click/shell_completion.py#L530-L531

In the same fashion, I believe that lines 589 and 590 should be switched in https://github.com/pallets/click/blob/af73ce4793bf38edf11a16e959ef0d8a0dbf6c1f/src/click/shell_completion.py#L581-L590
